children: on Wednesday reaffirmed its full-year aircraft delivery and production targets despite reporting third-quarter revenue below analysts’ expectations, raising the stakes for a year-end surge in jetliner handovers.

The European aerospace manufacturer maintained its goal of delivering approximately 870 commercial aircraft in 2026, which would mark an annual record. Airbus has delivered 547 planes through September, leaving it needing to hand over another 323 aircraft in the fourth quarter to meet its target.

Third-quarter revenue declined 2% to €17.47 billion ($20 billion), missing the €17.91 billion consensus estimate compiled by Airbus. Adjusted operating profit totaled €1.77 billion, broadly matching analysts’ expectations.

The results put greater emphasis on Airbus’ ability to convert its aircraft backlog into deliveries before year-end. For investors, meeting the annual target is important because aircraft handovers generate substantial cash receipts, making fourth-quarter production and delivery performance critical to the company’s profitability and cash flow.

Free cash flow before customer financing was negative €1.27 billion for the first nine months of 2026, reflecting an accumulation of inventory as Airbus prepared to accelerate aircraft deliveries and increase production toward year-end.

The company said supply-chain constraints have begun to ease, although component shortages and delivery delays remain challenges. Airbus has previously lowered annual delivery forecasts late in the year after disruptions involving engines and other aircraft components prevented it from meeting production schedules.

Chief Executive Guillaume Faury reaffirmed the company’s commitment to meeting its operational objectives while maintaining manufacturing quality, despite geopolitical uncertainty and ongoing supply-chain pressures.
Airbus maintains delivery lead over Boeing
Airbus continues to outpace rival Boeing

in commercial aircraft deliveries, having handed over 547 jets in the first nine months compared with Boeing’s 475. The U.S. manufacturer warned Tuesday that production disruptions and supply-chain difficulties would prevent it from meeting certain manufacturing and delivery targets this year.

Ronan Murphy, a director at Alton Aviation Consultancy, told Reuters that investors would be watching closely to determine whether Airbus can achieve its 870-aircraft target or will be forced to revise its outlook in December. Although supplier delays have moderated, he cautioned that production bottlenecks haven't been fully resolved.

title: Airbus maintains 2026 delivery target, setting up record Q4 push
